title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.

labels.sepsis: Sepsis, organism not identified, no organ dysfunction
labels.severe_sepsis: Severe sepsis with kidney injury, no shock

describe.sepsis: Admitted with sepsis due to pneumonia; blood cultures grew no organism. No acute organ dysfunction occurred; treated with IV antibiotics.
describe.severe_sepsis: Admitted with severe sepsis due to pneumonia with acute kidney injury caused by the sepsis; no organism grew and there was no shock. Kidney function recovered.
describe.septic_shock: Admitted with sepsis due to pneumonia that progressed to septic shock needing vasopressors; no organism grew. Recovered.
describe.mssa_sepsis: Admitted with sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) from a skin infection; no acute organ dysfunction; treated with cefazolin.
describe.urosepsis: The physician documents 'urosepsis' for a patient admitted with fever and a urinary infection; the words sepsis or septic are not used anywhere else, and no organism is named.
describe.bacteremia: A blood culture drawn for a fever came back positive (bacteremia); the physician documents that the patient does not have sepsis. Treated with oral antibiotics.

note_rules.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.

overstated_severe.description: Added severe sepsis or septic shock without a documented associated organ dysfunction or shock.

missed_severe.description: Left out severe sepsis (R65.20) when an organ dysfunction caused by the sepsis is documented.

missed_shock.description: Coded severe sepsis without shock when septic shock is documented.

unspecified_organism.description: Used sepsis, unspecified organism when the organism is documented.

urosepsis_coded_sepsis.description: Coded sepsis for 'urosepsis' (a nonspecific term with no code: query the provider).

bacteremia_coded_sepsis.description: Coded sepsis for bacteremia that the provider says is not sepsis.

rules.explain: Sepsis with no organism identified and no organ dysfunction: A41.9 only (HCC 2).

wrong.why: No acute organ dysfunction is documented: no R65.2- code.

rules.explain: Severe sepsis: the sepsis code A41.9, plus R65.20 because an acute organ dysfunction (kidney injury) is caused by the sepsis; no shock.

wrong.why: The sepsis caused an acute organ dysfunction: add R65.20.

rules.explain: Septic shock is severe sepsis with circulatory failure: A41.9 plus R65.21.

wrong.why: Septic shock is documented: R65.21, not R65.20.

rules.explain: Sepsis due to methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus: A41.01 (HCC 2).
'Urosepsis' is a nonspecific term with no default code and is not the same as sepsis: query the provider. No sepsis code.

wrong.why: Urosepsis is not sepsis; it needs a provider query.

rules.explain: Bacteremia without sepsis is coded R78.81 (no HCC), which is not a sepsis code: no sepsis code applies.

wrong.why: The provider documents bacteremia without sepsis.
